comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: This partial curriculum includes the confirmed first year and the credit-bearing components shared by the published upper-year schedules.
components: AI in Society: Safety, Regulation, Fairness
Study and Career Orientation for AI (Semester 1)
Study and Career Orientation for AI (Semester 2)
An individual supervised AI research project includes literature study, a method, implementation and evaluation, and a thesis in English. Entry requires completion of the first and second years.

audience.programmeDescription: Artificial Intelligence at the University of Amsterdam combines mathematics and computing with the study of cognition, language and how intelligent systems learn.

curriculum.limitation: This partial curriculum shows the confirmed 60 EC first year and 96 EC shared by the later-year schedules. The remaining 24 EC, including the final elective allowance, depend on the upper-year requirements for September 2026 entrants.

componentNotes.y1-01: Studies functions, limits, derivatives, integrals and Taylor approximations, including functions of several variables.
componentNotes.y1-02: Examines major developments in information science and their historical, scientific and social significance.
componentNotes.y1-03: Develops academic writing, presenting, critical discussion, teamwork and reflection through assignments linked to first-year AI study.
componentNotes.y1-04: Introduces programming through functions, data structures, classes, implementation exercises and code review.
componentNotes.y1-05: Develops vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalue methods and least-squares modelling for AI.
componentNotes.y1-06: Introduces convexity, linear and integer programming, nonlinear optimization and selected search methods.
componentNotes.y1-07: Uses computational models of human learning and decision-making, including reinforcement learning and choice models implemented in Python.
componentNotes.y1-08: Develops probability distributions, estimation, simulation and Bayesian statistical reasoning.
componentNotes.y1-09: Continues academic writing and presentation practice, including literature research, a research proposal and a technical report.
componentNotes.y1-10: Develops symbolic AI problem solving through Prolog, recursion, state-space search and analysis of algorithms.
componentNotes.y1-11: Introduces learning from examples and experience, using mathematical and statistical foundations to develop and assess models.
componentNotes.y1-12: Examines AI safety, regulation, fairness, privacy, accountability and societal effects through discussion and group work.
componentNotes.y2-01: Develops neural-network principles and architectures, training and evaluation, including convolutional, recurrent and transformer models.
componentNotes.y2-03: Develops communication, collaboration and professional exploration while helping students consider their third-year choices.
componentNotes.y2-04: Develops statistical and neural models of language, their implementation and evaluation, and ethical questions about language technology.
componentNotes.y2-06: Develops machine-learning pipelines, data processing, debugging, profiling, deployment and management of the model lifecycle.
componentNotes.y2-07: Uses graphical models to represent uncertainty, infer relationships and learn parameters, with programming applications.
componentNotes.y2-08: Develops data structures, algorithm design, complexity and correctness, with applications to AI problems.
componentNotes.y2-09: Continues academic and career preparation through writing, professional interviews, reflection and application skills.
componentNotes.y2-10: Develops computational models for image features, recognition, geometry and tracking, implemented in Python.
componentNotes.y2-12: A small team develops and documents an AI project with an external company. Available projects and participating companies vary each year.
componentNotes.y3-01: At least 30 EC of elective space is shared by the published schedules. The final allowance for September 2026 entrants remains unconfirmed.
componentNotes.y3-02: Connects epistemology, philosophy of science, philosophy of mind and ethics to foundational questions about AI.
componentNotes.y3-04: An individual supervised AI research project includes literature study, a method, implementation and evaluation, and a thesis in English. Entry requires completion of the first and second years.
